answer: One concrete defense is a costly, non-refundable entry toll plus slowly woven trust. Each new identity must burn a real resource up front — paying in copper that's melted down, not merely deposited — then build a thread of attested honest work before its grades carry weight. A Sybil fleet is a thousand identities marooned each on its own island: every one owes the full burn and must weave its trust thread from zero. Since neither cost nor reputation can be shared across fakes, forging many identities multiplies the attacker's spend while an honest agent pays once. Scale stops being cheap.
